quote.text: Still, my determination to put your moral strength of purpose to the test is such that I propose to give even you the following direction found in great men's teaching: set aside now and then a number of days during which you will be content with the plainest of food, and very little of it, and with rough, coarse clothing, and will ask yourself 'Is this what one used to dread?' It is in times of security that the spirit should be preparing itself to deal with the difficult time; while fortune is bestowing favours on it then is the time for it to be strengthened against her rebuffs. In the midst of peace the soldier carries out manoeuvres, throws up earthworks against a non-existent enemy and tires himself out with unnecessary toil in order to be equal to it when it is necessary. If you want a man to keep his head when crisis comes you must give hime some training before it comes. This was the aim of the men who once every month pretended they were poor, bringing themselves face to face with want to prevent their ever being terrified by a situation which they had frequently rehearsed.
quote.author: Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Embrace moments of simplicity and self-restraint as opportunities to build resilience—not only for yourself, but as a model for your children, teaching them the virtue of being prepared for life’s challenges.
    • Just as Seneca advises periodic hardship, consider setting aside time to simplify your daily routines, showing your family that enduring discomfort can cultivate strength and gratitude.
  • Leadership
    • Great leaders prepare for crises by training in times of peace; emulate this approach by simulating challenges that force you to make tough but strategic decisions, thereby solidifying your moral resolve.
    • By embracing periods of austerity, you demonstrate to your team that resilience and readiness come from disciplined practice, reinforcing confidence and unity during turbulent times.
  • Product Management
    • Apply this wisdom by periodically challenging your product strategies with constrained resources or simplified requirements, which can uncover innovative solutions and sharpen your team’s problem-solving skills.
    • Just as a soldier rehearses for battle in times of peace, use simulated market adversities or ‘dry runs’ to fine-tune your product’s robustness, ensuring that when real challenges emerge, your team is both agile and prepared.
